baseline.note: Re-verified at the v6.8.1 -> v6.8.3 sync (74 upstream commits, merge fb89d087a). The six pre-existing trees are byte-count IDENTICAL to the previous baseline (dtrh 1542, fyp 8, goon 184, intake 2138, player 3, tunnel 9, vendor 9), so no disposition changed. ONE NEW TREE ARRIVED: arcademy, 88 files, served upstream by Services/Arcademy/ArcademyHostService.cs. It is recorded not-ported with a board row - this guard is exactly the instrument that caught it, which is the second time it has caught a new upstream product surface arriving silently (the first was web/goon/, 184 files, with the suite green). Previous baseline: v6.8.0 / merge db3e842f (2026-08-14). Guard: client/tests/CcpClient.Tests/UpstreamPayloadInventoryTests.cs. A tree not listed here FAILS the suite; a listed tree that no longer exists upstream FAILS the suite. fileCountAtBaseline is record data, not an assertion (in-tree count drift is pinned by the per-tree manifest tests).

trees.name: arcademy
trees.boardRow: Decide the port's disposition for the Arcademy upstream surface [P1 OPEN]
trees.note: New at v6.8.3. Upstream Services/Arcademy/ArcademyHostService.cs and ArcademyMetaStore.cs render Resources/web/arcademy/ (a three.js campus shell: classes, ceremonies, report cards, split-flap board, keybinds, peek, audio). Zero references to 'arcademy' exist anywhere under client/ - the port has no host, no serving root and no payload glob for it. It also reaches the app-wide remote-media subsystem (FypOnlineCoordinator.For at ArcademyHostService.cs:1513), which is why the FYP census consumer set moved from 17 to 18 at this sync.
